claims: Rollover crashes account for nearly one-third of all traffic deaths.
Rollover crashes are most common in SUVs, pickups, and trucks.
A rollover crash definition is that the vehicle rotates 90 degrees or more, landing on its side or top.
Tripped rollovers account for 95% of single-vehicle rollovers.
Tripped rollovers occur when a vehicle leaves the roadway and strikes an object (curb, guardrail, ditch) or soft soil, causing it to flip.
Untripped rollovers are caused by reckless steering or high-speed maneuvers that force the vehicle to lose grip and flip.
Untripped rollovers are common in taller vehicles with higher centers of gravity.
Speeding is the primary factor in rollover crashes.
Over 70% of fatal rollovers occur in speed zones of 55 mph or higher.
SUVs, pickups, and vans are more prone to rollovers due to their higher center of gravity.
Rollover accidents are more common on rural roads
